clue.text: Harvest queen captured by Constable

indicators.note: the queen is held inside the policeman, as a prisoner is taken by an officer

parts.note: a constable is a police officer, informally a cop
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch is arrested by a village policeman at harvest time.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter John Constable, famous for harvest scenes, but here it is just a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop is the yield of grain or produce gathered from a field in one season.

clue.text: Volume of reduced car parking by a large town

indicators.note: the word car is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: The volume of traffic is cut thanks to car parks near a big town.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the amount a container can hold, its internal volume.

clue.text: Norma, perhaps, gets a rope tangled

indicators.note: a tangled rope is twisted up, so its letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Norma gets caught up in a knotted rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma looks like a woman's name; it is Bellini's opera, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is an example of an opera, the bel canto work by Vincenzo Bellini.

clue.text: Unknown mix of people deprived of oxygen in airship

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

indicators.note: the letters of the shortened word are mixed into a new order
the word for people loses the letter standing for oxygen

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange crowd of passengers finds itself short of air aboard an airship.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid German airship, named after Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin.

clue.text: Broken internet meant making up leisure activities

indicators.note: the words are broken apart and put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A broken internet connection meant people found other ways to pass the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment covers amusements and shows that people enjoy in their free time.

clue.text: Tower of nameless synthetic material put under pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, the shortened material is placed below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics

indicators.note: the material goes without the letter standing for name

parts.note: nylon is a synthetic fibre

explanation.surface: A tower built from anonymous plastic is under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice tower that carries overhead power cables.

clue.text: Permit union organisation before everyone finally leaves

parts.note: to let is to allow or permit
the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is the federation of British trade unions

indicators.note: only the final letter of everyone is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Allow the union body to meet before the last members walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb for people departing; it is a noun, the salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a salad plant eaten for its green leaves.

clue.text: Back-to-back refusals for a time

parts.note: no is a refusal, and two of them are needed

indicators.note: the two refusals are set back to back, so the second one faces the other way

explanation.surface: Saying no twice in a row, one refusal after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock, a particular moment of the day.

clue.text: Avenge bombing in Swiss location

indicators.note: the word avenge is blown apart and its letters reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A revenge bombing takes place in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a city in Switzerland, on the lake of the same name.

clue.text: Gift's here

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in attendance, as when answering a roll call

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a cheerful announcement that a gift has arrived; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for something given and an adjective for being in attendance.

clue.text: Release toy that's time consuming

indicators.note: the toy eats up the letter for time, taking it inside

parts.note: Lego is the plastic building-brick toy

explanation.surface: A toy that eats up hours is put out on release.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time consuming' reads as the familiar phrase for something slow, but it is split: time is the letter, consuming the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To let go of something is to stop holding it, to free or release it.

clue.text: Irish county's lake borne in mind

indicators.note: the lake is carried inside the word for mind, like something borne in a vessel

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'

explanation.surface: A sentimental line about keeping an Irish county's lake in one's thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borne in mind' reads as the idiom for remembering, but it splits: borne in is the container signal and mind gives the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare is a county on the west coast of Ireland, home of the Cliffs of Moher.

clue.text: Become exhausted and leave quickly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: hurry out of a place, as in running out of the room

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of someone fleeing in exhaustion; each half is a separate meaning of the same phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to be used up completely and to exit a place at speed.

clue.text: Secretive and quiet, grabbing duck and coot's tail

indicators.note: the word for quiet grabs and holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a shy person is quiet and reserved
a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: the tail of the word coot is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sneaky hunter quietly catches a duck and the tail of a coot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secretive and quiet' looks like a pair of definitions; only the first defines, and quiet is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means acting covertly, sly and unobserved, which is a secretive way of behaving.

clue.text: Decline leadership to shock constituency

parts.note: to take aback is to surprise or startle someone
in British politics a constituency is a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: A politician turns down the party leadership in order to stun the voters back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a back seat is the idiom for stepping aside and letting others lead or take charge.

clue.text: Bone Ken fractured with backward step

indicators.note: fractured like a broken bone, so the letters of Ken are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for step is written backwards

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A man called Ken breaks a bone stepping backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap, or patella, is the small bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: Tacky set of clothes for sport before school

parts.note: a sports kit is the outfit worn for a game

explanation.surface: A tasteless sports outfit is worn before school.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes art or objects in showy, sentimental bad taste, which is what tacky means.

clue.text: Broadcast famous cook showing how eggs may be prepared

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out on air, so the cook's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Mrs Isabella Beeton wrote the classic Victorian Book of Household Management

explanation.surface: A celebrity chef on television demonstrates how to prepare eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton was the famous Victorian British cookery writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are often whisked or beaten before scrambling or baking, so the past participle describes their preparation.

clue.text: Device for measuring minutes in a row

indicators.note: the letter for minutes is placed inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats in a stadium

explanation.surface: A gadget times how many minutes pass in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measuring minutes' runs on naturally, but the definition stops at 'measuring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A timer is a gadget that counts down or records elapsed time.

clue.text: Electrical engineer's shocking tales

indicators.note: shocking stirs up the word tales, and also nods to electric shocks

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inventor's stories are scandalous, or full of electric shocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' fits the electrical theme so well that it reads as description, yet it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor who pioneered alternating current systems.

clue.text: Laceration made by small whip

parts.note: a lash is a whip or a stroke from one

explanation.surface: A cut made by a little whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A slash is a long cut or gash in the skin, a laceration.

clue.text: Papa left us a sign

parts.note: P is papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Father left the family a sign before he went.
explanation.definitionFit: The plus is the mathematical symbol for addition, a cross-shaped sign.

clue.text: Doctor abridged column for her stand-in?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the shortened letters are rearranged
abridged means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper column is cut for a stand-in writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person needing cover, which is what the definition then refers to as 'her'.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a temporary substitute, typically a doctor or cleric covering for an absent colleague.

clue.text: Charm of some French antiques

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

parts.note: the run of letters lies across the end of French and the start of antiques

explanation.surface: Collectors are captivated by the charm of a few French antiques.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchant is to delight or bewitch, as a spell or a charm does.

clue.text: Individual imitates backsliding judge

indicators.note: sliding backwards means the word for imitates is written in reverse

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A lone figure copies a judge who has fallen back into bad habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate as an adjective means distinct or individual, existing apart from others.

clue.text: The reason to drink last of horrible watery residue

indicators.note: the word for the reason swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: why asks for the reason

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word horrible is used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks why anyone would drink a horrible watery leftover.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the thin liquid left behind when milk curdles and the curds are taken out in cheesemaking.
